capital_categories.method: Distribution (and, in New York, transmission) net plant growth split by the forward model's bau_plan.category_shares for this utility (growth / replacement / gridmod / other; status as in the utility JSON). Storm and resilience spending is not separable in Form 1 and sits inside replacement; IT and other = general and intangible plant (Form 1) plus the "other" share.

rr_bridge.note: Revenue requirement on a Form 1 functional basis for 2021 and 2025 (return on functional rate base at the allowed after-tax WACC, depreciation, O&M, taxes other than income, income taxes; general, intangible and A&G costs allocated to the scope by plant or O&M share; jurisdictional share applied), then the approved 2026 rate-case step. Computed in engine/lookback.py with the forward model's revenue-requirement structure.

property_tax_attribution.method: Plant-related property tax = the property tax / net plant ratio (Form 1 page 262 property and real estate taxes charged, all departments, / Form 1 page 200 net utility plant, all departments) x the scope's functional rate-base plant (scope net plant + allocated general and intangible plant, after the jurisdictional share). Property tax is assessed on plant value, so a uniform ratio attributes it to plant in proportion to net book value; assessed values, local rates and special-franchise valuation differ by plant type and locality, so this is an attribution, not a measured split. Non-plant taxes = the scope's taxes other than income (as in the detailed bridge) - plant-related property tax (payroll, gross receipts, franchise, sales and use and other taxes).

om_normalisation.check: Driven by pension and retiree-benefit credits: Form 1 account 926 (employee pensions and benefits) moves from $190.8M (2021) to $-386.5M (2025), a $577.4M swing, more than the whole $441.4M fall in administrative and general costs ($556.8M to $115.4M). CECONY's non-service components turn from a cost of $128M (2021) to a credit of $733M (2025) as expected returns on plan assets exceed interest cost and actuarial gains are recognised. The grouped view uses O&M normalised to exclude them.
om_normalisation.method: Normalised O&M = reported O&M (Form 1 functional basis) - non-service pension and retiree-benefit costs in administrative and general, allocated to the scope by the same O&M share as the rest of A&G and then by the jurisdictional share. The detailed bridge keeps reported O&M; the grouped view uses normalised O&M and shows the non-service change as its own reconciling line.

2021.source: Con Edison 2021 Form 10-K (filed 17 Feb 2022), Note E (CECONY total periodic benefit cost $451M, service cost including administrative expenses $321M) and Note F (CECONY total periodic postretirement benefit cost $14M, service cost $16M); electric share = CECONY electric other operations and maintenance $1,919M / CECONY total $2,452M (Results of Operations, 2021)
2021.notes: CECONY non-service pension and retiree-benefit cost (total periodic cost less service cost, pension + OPEB) = $128M company-wide x electric share 0.7826. Recorded in Form 1 account 926 (administrative and general); GAAP presents it outside operating income, which is why the 10-K's O&M does not fall. Before the rate-level reconciliation (the deferral of the difference from the rate allowance), which stays in O&M.

2025.source: Con Edison 2025 Form 10-K (filed 19 Feb 2026), Note E (CECONY total periodic benefit credit $(545)M, service cost including administrative expenses $158M) and Note F (CECONY total periodic postretirement benefit credit $(21)M, service cost $9M); electric share = CECONY electric other operations and maintenance $2,614M / CECONY total $3,394M (Results of Operations, 2025)
2025.notes: CECONY non-service pension and retiree-benefit cost (total periodic cost less service cost, pension + OPEB) = $-733M company-wide x electric share 0.7702. Recorded in Form 1 account 926 (administrative and general); GAAP presents it outside operating income, which is why the 10-K's O&M does not fall. Before the rate-level reconciliation (the deferral of the difference from the rate allowance), which stays in O&M.
